name: fix_cpp_memory_leak
description: Fixes a C++ class whose destructor leaks memory and never decrements its live-instance counter
prompts: The header buffer.h defines a class `Buffer` that is meant to manage a dynamically allocated array and track how many instances currently exist via the static counter `Buffer::instance_count` (incremented whenever a Buffer is constructed). Right now, `instance_count` never goes back down after a Buffer object is destroyed - even after every Buffer object has gone out of scope, `Buffer::instance_count` stays at whatever it peaked at, and the memory allocated in the constructor is never released. Fix the destructor `~Buffer()` so that destroying a Buffer object properly frees its allocated memory and decrements `instance_count` by one, without changing the public interface (the constructor signature `Buffer(int size)` and the member name `instance_count` must stay the same).

test_setup_files.test_leak.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['g++', '-std=c++17', 'test_leak_main.cpp', '-o', 'test_leak_bin'], check=True)
proc = subprocess.run(['./test_leak_bin'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'leak test failed: exit {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-300:]}'
assert 'PASS' in proc.stdout
print('PASS')
